'''Bodo Illgner''' ({{IPA|de|ˈboːdoː ˈʔɪlɡnɐ}}; born 7 April 1967) is a German former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].
During his career he played for [[1. FC Köln]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], and helped [[Germany national football team|Germany]] to the [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990 World Cup]], where he became the first goalkeeper to keep a [[Shutout|clean sheet]] in a [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] final.

==Club career==
[[File:Bodo Illgner.jpg|thumb|Illgner in 1996]]
Born in [[Koblenz]], Illgner was a product of [[1. FC Köln]]'s youth system, and made his debut in the [[Bundesliga]] on 22 February 1986 at not yet 19, in a 3–1 away loss against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]. From the [[1987–88 Bundesliga|1987–88 season]] onwards, he became the club's undisputed starter – as successor of [[Harald Schumacher]] in both 1. FC Köln and the Germany national team – being voted as [[Best European Goalkeeper]] in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/illgnerdata.html|title=Bodo Illgner – Matches and Goals in Bundesliga|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|first=Matthias|last=Arnhold|date=23 September 2015|access-date=9 October 2015}}</ref>

On 30 August 1996, already having started the campaign with Köln, Illgner was signed by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], and played 40 [[La Liga]] matches in [[1996–97 La Liga|his first year]] to help the [[Madrid|capital]] side to the national championship conquest. In [[1997–98 La Liga|the following]] he lost his place to [[Santiago Cañizares]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/1998/enero/31/deportes/realmadrid.html|title=Se agranda la portería del Real Madrid|trans-title=Real Madrid goal gets larger|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es|date=31 January 1998|access-date=19 May 2016}}</ref> but regained it in time to play in [[1998 UEFA Champions League Final|the final]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]] against [[Juventus F.C.|Juventus FC]] (1–0 win).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=1997/overview/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016130558/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=1997/overview/|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 October 2015|title=1997/98: Seventh heaven for Madrid|publisher=UEFA|date=20 May 1998|access-date=17 January 2016}}</ref>

In [[1999–2000 La Liga|1999–2000]], Illgner was succeeded by 18-year-old [[Iker Casillas]], after which he retired from football altogether.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2001/08/08/mas_futbol/997322785_850215.html|title=Bodo Illgner se retira del fútbol|trans-title=Bodo Illgner retires from football|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=8 August 2001|access-date=17 January 2016}}</ref>

In April 2013, he was named by [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] as a member of the "Best foreign eleven in [[History of Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid's history]]".<ref name="best-foreign"/>

==International career==
On 23 September 1987, Illgner made his debut for the [[Germany national football team|West Germany national team]] in a 1–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] home win against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]], and went on to back [[Eike Immel]] during [[UEFA Euro 1988]]. At the [[1990 FIFA World Cup]] he, by now the country's first-choice, was in exceptional form, and commanded the backline which consisted of the experienced [[Klaus Augenthaler]], [[Andreas Brehme]], [[Thomas Berthold]], [[Guido Buchwald]] and [[Jürgen Kohler]] (with [[Matthias Sammer]] taking Augenthaler's place at [[UEFA Euro 1992|Euro 1992]]); in the semi-final, he saved a [[Stuart Pearce]] shot in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] against [[England national football team|England]], and his team would overcome [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in [[1990 FIFA World Cup Final|the deciding match]], where he would keep a [[Shutout#Association football)|clean sheet]] in the 1–0 success.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/1717/editorial/2009/02/17/1114350/where-are-they-now-germanys-1990-world-cup-winners|title=Where are they now? Germany's 1990 World Cup winners|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Mathew|last=Burt|date=17 February 2009|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

Overall, Illgner appeared 54 times for his country, and also played at the [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994 World Cup]], surprisingly retiring after the quarter-final loss against [[Bulgaria national football team|Bulgaria]] although he was only 27.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/illgner-intl.html|title=Bodo Illgner – International Appearances|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|first=Matthias|last=Arnhold|date=23 September 2015|access-date=9 October 2015}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
Illgner later went on to work as a [[pundit]] for [[Sky Deutschland]] and English language broadcasts of [[beIN Sports]].<ref name="best-foreign">{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/04/11/en/football/real_madrid/1365709938.html|title=The best foreign eleven in Real Madrid's history|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=12 April 2013|access-date=25 August 2013}}</ref>
